newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels give Mobutu forces Sunday deadline.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels give Mobutu forces Sunday deadline.

text.p: Zaire's victorious rebels in their first radio broadcast in Kinshasa ordered defeated government troops to report by Sunday morning and warned looters they would be severely punished.
Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) captured the capital on Saturday from remaining loyalists of departed President Mobutu Sese Seko.

"Soldiers or other armed elements are instructed to report tomorrow (Sunday) morning at the latest at the following command posts of the Alliance forces," the statement said, naming two military barracks.
"The population is required to denounce those armed elements who have not reported voluntarily," the statement added.
The statement, read in French and the local Lingala language, said Mobutu's dictatorial regime had been totally defeated in Kinshasa after 30 years of oppression.
"Acts of vandalism, theft and looting are completely forbidden and will in future be severely punished," it said.
Looters attacked the wealthy Binza suburb on Saturday before rebels arrived there, residents said.
The statement referred throughout to "Congo" and "Congolese", confirming Kabila's decision to abolish the name Zaire, adopted by Mobutu in 1971.
Kabila was expected to arrive in Kinshasa from his southern headquarters at Lubumbashi in the next few days, rebel sources said.
